etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Originally derived as the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb よる (yoru, “to arise from, to start from”), spelled variously in kanji as 因る, 依る, 由る, etc..

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Calque of European grammatical constructions such as English more, leveraging the sense “from, beyond, past” sense of the particle.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 寄(よ)る (yoru, “to approach, to draw near”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 縒(よ)る (yoru, “to twist, to entwine”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 拠(よ)る (yoru, “to be based on, to depend on”), 因(よ)る (yoru, “to be due to, to be caused by”).
